What I loved about skating as a teenager: What I loved about dance as a teenager also pulled me into coaching: the urge to keep moving, experimenting, refining, and growing, all while supported by a community doing the same. Fifteen years later, that spirit still fuels me as a Nashville-based mobility coach.
My path here hasn’t been the traditional: My path here hasn’t been the traditional one — I got hurt young, rebuilt my own body in a small town with no real gym, and learned how to coach people through pain while juggling tight schedules and the pressure I put on myself to get every detail right. Along the way, I discovered that big numbers, fancy gear, and fast results don’t define a member’s progress — it’s how they move and how they feel getting there.
Whether it’s a scrappy shoot or a nation: Whether it’s a stiff desk worker or a state-level lifter, my approach stays the same: breath first, patience always, grit through it all.
When I’m not on set, you’ll find me hang: When I’m not on the floor, you’ll find me hanging out with my three kids, losing at chess, or seeing if I can still hold a handstand at 36.
Past collaborations include Xfinity, Cum: Past work includes physical therapy clinics, Nashville SC youth teams, local dance studios, and two running clubs.
The first time I did a commercial as jus: The first time I ran a full class of twenty on my own. I’d been brought in early enough to help shape the program with the head coach and plan every block so I knew exactly what we needed. Of course, things came up on the day, but we pivoted, I trusted my gut, and pulled it together in the cooldown. I got to coach an amazing group, a loud crowd, a DJ — the works. Even though everyone was working super hard, and I had prepped like crazy, it felt like I was just doing cool stuff with my friends. That combo of camaraderie and grit is why I love this job.

The short film, &quot;Thought of You,&qu: The Turkish get-up blew me away when I first learned it 14 years ago, and it still does. In modern training, we can be incredibly flashy, throw complex circuits in people's faces, add bands and chains all over the place, and bring tons of energy to a session. And I love that. But this lift reminds me that simplicity can be just as powerful. I also keep going back to the deep goblet squat. The patience, the breathing, the way it shows you exactly where you're stuck… It’s beautiful. I love heavy lifting, and that’s in the background, but it brings the basics of good movement out in a really beautiful way. Yeah, it’s a warm-up move. Sue me.

Jacob Frost is a Detroit-born director w: Dre Collins is a Memphis-born coach whose work carries the influence of Southern grit and quiet, steady patience. Starting his career in Knoxville, he built a foundation in sports performance and physical therapy, focusing on training that feels honest and simple. Informed by a background in music and a teacher at heart, Dre’s approach prioritizes rhythm, breathing, and technique, creating sessions that balance hard work with real-world recovery. His feel for pacing and load lets members progress naturally, giving his programs a steady, lasting weight. Dre now coaches the 5AM Club and the conditioning program, working with members and teams to build training that feels both serious and human. Whether working with a full class or one-on-one with an athlete coming back from injury, his process stays rooted in observation, consistency, and a hands-on coaching style shaped by the work ethic and patience of the South.
Getting the perfect performance on the f: Getting the perfect rep on the first try is great, but working for it is far more rewarding. I’ll never forget coaching a dad through his first pull-up after six months of trying. He needed the smallest change in his grip and his breath, and on attempt eight, we finally found it.
I’d probably be a prop fabricator. I gre: I’d probably be a carpenter. I grew up in awe of my dad’s workbench, and his tools were an early resource that built my first squat rack. I still enjoy building my own equipment for the gym and hope to eventually get deeper into the craft.
Knives Out is easily my most rewatched f: The front squat is easily my most repeated lift. It manages to be both humbling and fun at the same time. And our 5AM playlist has made it into my Spotify Wrapped every year since we started the class.
